full_judgment:
This Rule arises out of an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against the judgment and decree dated 20-10-1993 passed by the District Judge, Netrokona in other class Appeal No.127 of 1989 affirming those dated 14-6-1989 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge Netrokona in other class suit No. 82 of 1988 dismissing the suit. 

 2. The petitioner as plaintiff filed a suit being other class suit No. 82 of 1988 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Netrokona against the opposite parties impleading them as defendants for two declarations to the effect that the appointment of defendant No.1 as permanent Kazi for Barhatta Union Parishad is illegal, void and for a decree for permanent injunction against the defendant No.1 so that he cannot act as a permanent Kazi for Barhatta Union under the District of Netrokona. 

 4. The defendants contested the suit by filing 2 sets of written statements contending, inter-alia, that the defendant No.3 invited applications from the permanent resident of Barhatta Union Parishad for appointment of permanent Kazi for the said Parishad along with other union parishads under the district of Netrokona. In response to the notification the plaintiff, the defendant No.1 and two other persons applied for appointment of permanent Kazi of the said Union Parishad. The Interview Board interviewed the plaintiff No. 1 and 2 other persons but did not call for any interview of defendant No.1. After holding interview the selection Board recommended the 3 candidates showing the name of plaintiff No.1 in serial No.1 as he stood first in the interview. On receipt of the recommendation from the Interview Board government asked the plaintiff to submit certificates showing that he has requisite qualification for appointment of a permanent Kazi but he failed to furnish, the requisite certificates showing that he has the requisites qualification for his appointment as a permanent Kazi. For various reasons the other two persons were also not appointed as permanent Kazi. The Government then asked the defendant No.1 to submit the necessary papers to show that he has the requisite qualification for appointment of permanent Kazi and after examining the papers submitted by the defendant No.1 the Government was satisfied as to his qualification and thereafter appointed him as a permanent Kazi for Barhatta Union Parishad along with other union parishads for the district of Netrokona. It is further asserted in the written statement that the plaintiff is not the son of Mahfiluddin the former Kazi of Barhatta Union Parishad and he is not a permanent resident of Barhatta Union Parishad. It is further asserted that the plaintiff did not obtain his Alim decree from any Madrasha which is approved by the Madrasha Board and, as such, he failed to qualify as a candidate for the appointment of permanent Kazi. They further asserted that, in fact, his father''s name is Mafizuddin and he is now dead and he is permanent resident of village Birampur within Mohongonj Upazila in the district of Netrokona. The plaintiff has passed Alim examination from Mohanganj Zamia, Kashinlia Kowmia Madrasha which is not an affiliated Madrasha with the Madrasha Board and it is not an approved Madrasha. They further asserted that the defendant No.1 was called for by the interview board as candidate No.1 and the plaintiff appeared before the interview board by securing forged document but since he stood first before the interview board he was asked to file papers to show that he has requisite qualification for the said post but the plaintiff has failed to submit the necessary certificate to show that he has passed Alim examination from an approved Madrasha and thereafter the defendant No.4 in pursuance of the powers vested in the Government under section 14 of the Muslim Marriage and Nikanama Registration Act appointed the defendant No.1 as permanent Kazi for the Barhatta Union Parishad and directed the plaintiff to hand over charge to him. The plaintiff is a shrewd man and he in collusion with retired Kazi of Barhatta Union Parishad tried to get appointment as permanent Kazi but when it was disclosed that he was not qualified for temporary appointment then the appointment was legally canceled by the government and hence they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 5. The trial Court after examining the witnesses and hearing the arguments of both sides dismissed the suit vide his judgment and decree dated 14-6-1989. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the plaintiff-petitioner preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge which was registered as other class No.127 of 1989. The learned District Judge by the judgment and decree dated 20-10-1993 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree of the appellate Court below the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 7. It appears from the revision application that the first ground taken by the plaintiff-petitioner is that the defendant No.3 invited applications for regular appointment of Kazi for Barhatta Union Parishad vide his office Memo No. 9740(190) dated 21-9-1986 and it was only mentioned in the said memo that the candidates should be Aleem passed and it was not disclosed that the intending candidates should be from Alim Madrasha Board and, as such, the defendant No.4 committed an illegality in appointing the defendant opposite party No. 1 as permanent Kazi in place of the plaintiff-petitioner on the ground that he is a Alim decree holder from a private Madrasha. The second ground of the provisional application is that the Courts below erred in law in not considering that there is no difference between a Alim certificate issued from a Kowmee Madrasha and a similar certificate issued from Madrasha Board. It appears that the 3rd ground taken by the plaintiff-petitioner in the revisional application is that the Courts below erred in law in not considering that the plaintiff- petitioner was called for the interview and he stood first in the said interview and the interview committee prepared a panel of selected candidates for appointment accordingly, and the defendant No.1 was not called for the said interview and his name was not included in the panel and he is not supposed to get the appointment of Kazi of Barhatta Union Parishad. The further ground that is taken in the revisional application is that the defendant No.3 did not amend their Memo No.9740(190) dated 21-9-1986 to the effect that the intending candidates should be Alim passed from Madrasha Board. The final ground taken in the revisional application is that, the Courts below erred in law in not considering that as per provision of section 4 of the Muslim Marriage and Divorce Registration Act 1975, the advisory committee selected and recommended for appointment of the plaintiff-petitioner for the post of Kazi of Barhatta Union Parishad and as per normal procedure it is to be accepted by the Government. 

 9. On a perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the learned appellate Court below concurred with the findings of the trial Court that the plaintiff-petitioner is not a permanent resident of village Birampur within Mohangonj PS under district Netrokona but the appellate Court below rightly observed that in the notification of the defendant dated 21-9-1986 it was not disclosed that intending candidates must be a permanent resident of Barhatta. Union and, as such, that cannot be a valid ground for refusing appointment of the plaintiff-petitioner as permanent Kazi for this said Union Parishad, but the learned appellate Court below concurred with the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff-petitioner has failed to submit his certificate to show that he is a proper qualified person and obtained a Alim Decree from an approved Madrasha under the Madrasha Board and admittedly, he has obtained his decree from Kowmee Madrasha which is a private Madrasha and, as such, the Government did not appoint him as Kazi for the said Union Parishad although he stood first before the Selection Board and, as such, the learned appellate Court below concurred with the findings of the trial Court that the plaintiff-petitioner failed to show that he has obtained Alim Degree from any approved Madrasha under the Madrasha Board. On the other hand, the defendant opposite party No. 1 has shown that he obtained his Alim, Fazil and Kamil Decrees from an approved Madrashah under the Madrasha Board and, as such, on consideration of the certificates the Government was satisfied about his qualification and consequently appointed him as permanent Kazi for the said Barhatta Union Parishad along with other Union and this appointment given by the Government to the defendant opposite party No. 1 cannot be called illegal on any count whatsoever. The learned appellate Court below also concurred with the finding of the trial Court that since the plaintiff-petitioner has no requisite qualification to become a permanent Kazi, he has no legal right to challenge the appointment of defendant opposite party No. 1 and, as such, concurred with the findings of the trial Court that the plaintiff has no locus standi to file the instant suit. It is also found by the learned appellate Court below that the plaintiff-petitioner is, in fact, not the son of former Kazi Mahfiluddin but, in fact, he is the son of one late Mofizuddin but suppressing this fact he applied for the said post of Kazi of the said Barhatta Union Parishad stating himself as the son of Mohfiluddin, former Kazi of the said Barhatta Union Parishad, but when the fact was revealed he came up with a plea that he is an adopted son of said Mahfiluddin. Both the Courts below disbelieved the story that he is an adopted son of Mahfiluddin. Be that as it may, it may be mentioned here that Muhammadan Law does not provide for adoption of a son and, as such, this has no legal basis at all. The concurrent findings of the Courts below are that the plaintiff-petitioner has no requisite qualification for said post and the defendant opposite party No.1 has the requisite qualification and the Government, being satisfied about his qualification, has rightly appointed him as a permanent Kazi for the said Barhatta Union Parishad and, as such, the plaintiff-petitioner has no locus standi to file the instant suit. In arriving at such findings of fact the Courts below did not commit any illegality whatsoever and these concurrent findings of fact are based on materials and evidence on record. In that view of the matter, I find substance in the submissions made by Mr Md Ferozur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the defendant opposite party No.1.
